chunks: Ali, from Sahl, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I walk through the market and buy a khuff (leather sock), not knowing whether it is pure or not.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Pray in it.' I said, 'And what about the na'l (leather shoe)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Similar to that.' I said, 'I am constrained from this.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do you prefer to turn away from what Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to do?'

key_terms.أَعْتَرِضُ: I walk through / I browse (in the market)
key_terms.خُفّ: Leather sock or boot, a type of footwear worn over the foot and lower leg

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in shoes or socks of uncertain purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *istishab al-taharah* (presumption of purity), where Imam al-Rida (AS) validates praying in footwear of uncertain purity, countering excessive caution (*tatawwu'*). The Imam’s gentle rebuke highlights the Shia scholarly preference for ease in worship over rigid asceticism, encouraging believers to follow the practical precedent of the Imams rather than imposing unnecessary restrictions.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Sahl, from one of his companions, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘I see the market display, so I buy socks, not knowing whether it is pure or not’. Heasws said: ‘You can pray Salāt in it’. I said, ‘So (what about) the slippers?’ Heasws said: ‘Similar to that’. I said, ‘I am constrained from this’. Heasws said: ‘Would you turn away from what Abu Al-Hassanasws used to do?’
en.sarwar: 31. Ali has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain persons of his people from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I visit the market and buy a slipper but I do not know if it is from properly slaughtered animal or not. He (the Imam) said, ‘Perform Salah (prayer) with it.’ I then asked, ‘Can I use such shoes?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the same as slippers.’ I then said, ‘I am not comfortable with it.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you dislike what abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would do?”’
